caption: A bus drives slowly past a row of shop windows, and its reflection moves along in the glass beside it.

sa.check: A bus moves along a street.
A row of shop windows runs beside the street.
The bus's reflection is visible in the windows.
The reflection moves along with the bus.

pc.expect: The reflection travels with the bus, in step with it, and appears only in the glass: it stops where a pane ends and shows again in the next pane.
pc.fail: The reflection stays still while the bus moves; or moves in the opposite direction; or continues across the wall between windows; or the bus has no reflection in a plainly reflective window.

pc.expect: Nothing in the reflection moves that is not moving in reality; a stationary bus has a stationary reflection.
pc.fail: The reflection moves while the bus has stopped; or shows the bus in a different pose or heading; or people in the reflection move differently from those on the street.

pc.expect: The reflection is a mirror image of the bus: same colours and size, alongside the real bus, with any lettering reversed.
pc.fail: The reflection is a different vehicle or colour; or upside down; or far larger or smaller than the bus; or its lettering reads the right way round.

pc.expect: The windows are flat rigid panes: the reflection is undistorted and the shop interior is seen through it.
pc.fail: The glass ripples like water; or the reflection warps as it slides; or the window frames bend.

pc.expect: One bus and one reflection per pane; the bus does not pass through the windows and nothing appears or vanishes.
pc.fail: A second bus appears; or the bus drives into the glass; or the reflection steps out into the street; or the bus vanishes mid-pass.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The shop fronts, the bus livery and the street stay the same.
pc.fail: The bus's livery changes; or shop signs change; or the number of windows changes.
